chunks.text: Today, we will talk about Ethiopia.
Ethiopia is a beautiful, historic, and diverse country in East Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Ethiopia?
Ethiopia is in East Africa.
It is next to Eritrea, Sudan, South Sudan, Kenya, Somalia, and Djibouti.
It has no sea, but it has many mountains, rivers, and valleys.
What is the capital city of Ethiopia?
The capital city is Addis Ababa.
Addis Ababa is a big city in the center of the country.
It is home to the African Union and many international offices.
Other important cities in Ethiopia include Gondar with old castles, Lalabella with rock churches, Deridawa, McKell, and Bahirdar.
How many people live in Ethiopia?
About 120 million people live in Ethiopia.
It is the second most populated country in Africa.
There are many ethnic groups and languages.
Ethiopia is a very diverse country.
What language do people speak in Ethiopia?
Ethiopia has over 80 languages.
The official language is Amharic.
Other major languages include Oromo, Tigrinya, Somali, Afar.
Many people also speak English, especially in schools and cities.
What is the weather like in Ethiopia?
Ethiopia has different climates.
In the highlands, the weather is cool and fresh.
In the lowlands, it is hot and dry.
There are rainy seasons and dry seasons.
In Addis Ababa, the weather is mild all year.
What does Ethiopia look like?
Ethiopia has mountains like the Simeon Mountains, valleys and plateaus, the Great Rift Valley, lakes like Lake Tana, the largest in Ethiopia, rivers like the Blue Nile.
It is one of the most scenic countries in Africa.
What animals live in Ethiopia?
In Ethiopia, you can find lions, leopards, and hyenas, baboons, monkeys and warthogs, birds like eagles and ibis, unique animals like the Gelata Baboon and Wallya Ibex.
In the countryside, people raise goats, sheep, cows, and donkeys.
What do people eat in Ethiopia?
Ethiopian food is spicy, flavorful, and shared.
The most common food is injera, a sour, spongy flatbread.
People eat it with different stews called wat, popular dishes.
Dora wat, chicken stew with eggs.
Monsieur wat, spicy lentil stew.
Shiro, a chickpea stew.
Tibs, fried meat with onions and peppers.
People eat with their hands, using injera to pick up the food.
What do people drink in Ethiopia?
Ethiopia is the birthplace of coffee.
People love coffee -buna, often served in a coffee ceremony.
Tea, water and fruit juice.
Tella, a homemade traditional beer.
The Ethiopian Coffee Ceremony is a special tradition with family and guests.
What is life like in Ethiopia?
Life is different in cities and villages.
In cities, people go to work, school, and markets.
In rural areas, many people farm, herd animals, or make crafts.
People value family community, respect for elders, sharing food and time together.
Music, dance, and colorful clothes are part of everyday life.
What are some holidays and traditions in Ethiopia?
Angkutatash, Ethiopian New Year in September.
Meskel, a religious holiday with fire celebrations.
Timkit, celebrating epiphany with processions and water.
Fasika, Orthodox Easter Christmas.
Gina, celebrated on January 7th.
Ethiopia uses its own calendar and clock, which are different from Western systems.
Some fun facts about Ethiopia.
Ethiopia was never colonized except for a short Italian occupation.
It has its own alphabet called Gi's script.
The Ethiopian calendar has 13 months.
Many people in Ethiopia follow Orthodox Christianity, Islam, or other faiths.
The flag is green, yellow, and red.
Many African countries use these colors too.
Now you know many things about Ethiopia.
You know where it is, what people speak, and what they eat.
You learned about nature, cities, traditions, and daily life.
Great job!
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emili.
